Aba (Avka) Shreir, son of Itel and Mendel, was born in 1906 in Lithuania. In 1924 he immigrated to Eretz Israel and joined the Gedud HaAvoda (Labor Battalion) in Jerusalem as a quarryman. In 1926 he moved to Migdal, where he worked in agriculture and was active among the workers as a labor secretary and council member. He was alert to every public enterprise of the Histadrut (the General Federation of Labor) and took an active part in all its institutions. By day he did grueling work in the orchards, and in the evenings he worked on public projects. He was a member of the village committee and devoted himself warmly to the public affairs of the workers there. When he was offered a salary, he refused: "On our terms, a secretary who takes a wage cuts himself off from the public." He worked to obtain a plot of land for the building of the Histadrut house. From 1925 until the day he died, he served in the Haganah (the pre-state Jewish defense organization).

All his life he dreamed of settling the land, and even when his dream came true with the founding of the moshav Ein Vered in 1933, he did not forget his comrades in Migdal. At all times he would visit and show concern for their fate. His comrades affectionately called him "Avka."

On 2 Tammuz 5698 (5 July 1938), on his way to work with three of his comrades in the Pardes Yechin orchard near the moshav, they were fired upon from an ambush by members of an Arab gang. Aba and his comrade Mordechai were killed on the spot, and Sraga Orbach and Aryeh HaCohen were mortally wounded. Aba was laid to rest together with his three comrades in a mass grave at the Gush cemetery in Tel Mond. He left a wife and a daughter.

His name was commemorated in the book *Hem HaLchu* ("They Went"). Articles in memory of him were published in the newspapers.
